entries.original: The standalone `omo` binary starts about 4x faster on Linux and 6x faster on macOS: release binaries now carry Bun's bytecode cache, so a launch no longer parses the whole bundled program first (`omo --version` 880 ms -> 202 ms on Linux x64, 214 ms -> 33 ms on Apple silicon). Each binary is about 43 MB larger, and the per-binary size budget rises from 210 MiB to 260 MiB. ([#13464](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13464))

entries.original: A memory reflection or dream launcher now hears its supervisor's exit even when the supervisor dies while the "launched" receipt is still being written. The launcher used to subscribe to the exit only after that write, so an early supervisor death was never reported and the launcher waited for an outcome that could not arrive: until the run deadline (15 minutes by default), or without a deadline while the run was still queued. The run now fails at once with the supervisor's exit status. ([#13532](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13532)) ([#13563](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13563))

entries.original: An engine registers its agent dir with the device service again when the service stops and comes right back, whether or not the operating system reports the new socket in time. Once its connection had closed, the registrant used to wait for that file notification alone, and on a macOS machine with heavy file activity the notification arrived seconds to tens of seconds late, so the restarted service did not list that engine's sessions until then. The registrant now arms its endpoint watch again once the endpoint it knew is gone, so a service that is listening again within about a second of that is found by the watch's one-second re-check. A service that returns later than that still waits for the notification ([#13531](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/issues/13531)) ([#13530](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13530), fixes #12733). ([#13563](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13563))

entries.original: `omo remote send` in wait mode printed the previous turn's answer and returned before its own turn settled: the follow printed every `text_delta` it received and settled on the first `agent_settled`, including the attach's replayed history, which over the relay arrives only after `onEvent` returns. A send that started or steered a turn now streams its deltas from the aim on (whatever the attach replayed before the aim is dropped) and settles only at its run's `agent_settled`, so retries and queued follow-ups stream through; a queued send's answer is read from the session's transcript, anchored on the send's own user entry, final when a later message's turn supersedes it or a run settled with it as the tail. A waiting send carries its own `clientMessageId`, which senpi stamps on the user entry it stores, so the anchor holds when a prompt template or skill expansion rewrote that entry's text and never lands on an older send of the same text; an engine that stores no id falls back to the text match. entries.original: Memory sync settings: when sync cannot read its status, OmO now records WHY. The engine's status path kept one sentence, "Memory sync authority is unavailable.", for every cause, with nothing in the log, so a report of that screen could not be acted on. The device and pending-request reads and the enable and approve operations, which ended in the same sentence, now carry a code too (`operation_failed` for an unexpected error) and log it with the error; the reads, which the desktop also polls, log once per cause. entries.original: `thread_create { worktree: { branch?, base? } }` creates a git worktree for the new thread, on this device or another one, in OmO's worktrees folder there, and starts the thread in it; every failure (not a repository, branch or folder exists, unknown base, no disk space, no permission, git missing, an older omo on the other device) is a typed code with `details.reason` and a next action (#13408). A worktree whose thread then fails to open, or whose `git worktree add` fails part way (including git's timeout), is removed with its branch; what cannot be removed is named in a `partial_commit` failure (`worktree_left_behind`). The worktree request another device answers takes only absolute folders and removes only a worktree inside its own worktrees folder on the branch named. entries.original: Thread gateway: the store can take in a delivery that another device's service attested for a session on this device that is not running (the intake row of #13037). The row is committed in the same transaction as a same-device delivery, keeps the sender's delivery id, text and display text, is rate-limited per sending device, and is admitted later under the engine's own ledger key, so the engine counts it once even if the same delivery also arrives live. A repeat of a delivery id from the same device is answered with the first answer. A reply to such a delivery continues its chain.
